'''Philip Anthony Richard Hockey''' (8{{Nbsp}}March 1956{{Snd}}24{{Nbsp}}January 2013) was a well-known South African [[ornithologist]]. He was director of the [[Percy FitzPatrick Institute of African Ornithology]] at the [[University of Cape Town]], co-editor of ''[[Roberts' Birds of Southern Africa]]'' and co-author of ''[[Sasol Birds of Southern Africa]]''. Hockey was born in [[Bournemouth, England]] in 1956 and moved to South Africa in 1979. His doctoral study was on the [[African oystercatcher]]. He focused on shorebirds, writing the book ''Waders of Southern Africa''. Hockey observed 885 different species of birds in Southern Africa.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leading ornithologist Phil Hockey dies |url=http://www.news.uct.ac.za/article/-2013-01-25-leading-ornithologist-phil-hockey-dies |access-date=2022-10-21 |website=www.news.uct.ac.za |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ryan |first=Peter G. |date=2013-07-01 |title=Phil Hockey (1956–2013) |journal=Ibis |language=en |volume=155 |issue=3 |pages=698–700 |doi=10.1111/ibi.12058|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Little |first=Rob M |date=2015-05-04 |title=Special issue in memory of Philip Anthony Richard Hockey |journal=Ostrich |language=en |volume=86 |issue=1–2 |pages=iii–iv |doi=10.2989/00306525.2015.1046726 |s2cid=87456370 |issn=0030-6525|doi-access=free |bibcode=2015Ostri..86D...3L }}</ref>
